selection: 10 distinct records sampled uniformly without replacement from all 4,776 with Python secrets.SystemRandom().sample; no redraw or substitution.
limitations: This is a small answer-key spot-check, not validation of all questions, official paper provenance, or the Chemistry/Biology subsets. One pass requires original.mm to see the full question. The conditional record needs its original SVG and a stated g value.

records.working: With six balls hanging, a=(6/10)g; the three balls behind the 7th have mass 6 kg, so T=3.6g N. This is 36 N only for g=10 m/s^2; g is not specified in the captured stem. Its SVG is required to establish the numbering.
Re = rho*v*d/eta, which is dimensionless. This is option C (zero-based index 2).
Choose 2 of 10 digits, then use both in a 4-character string: C(10,2)*(2^4-2)=630. Independently enumerating all 10,000 PINs also gives 630.
Opposite sides subtract: Rx=P-5P=-4P and Ry=3P-2P=P. Magnitude sqrt(17)*P is option A.

Read the actual column content from original.mm. A: posterior probability of five white balls=(1)/(1+2+3+4+5)=1/3=p/9, so p=3. B: sum k^2*C(9,k)=9*10*2^7, so m=9. C: f(t)=10t/(2-t) has f′′(t)=40/(2-t)^3>0, so Jensen gives minimum 3*f(1/3)=6. D: 10*k*C(10,k)*C(9,k-1)=100*C(9,k-1)^2; Vandermonde gives 100*C(18,9), yielding p=5. Column indices are [0,4,2,1]. The key is correct, but Study Buddy has no grid renderer.
kx=m*omega^2*(l+x) gives x=m*l*omega^2/(k-m*omega^2), option B. A finite positive stretch requires k>m*omega^2.
Ring about diameter, disk about central normal and solid cylinder about its axis each have I=MR^2/2. A solid sphere has I=2MR^2/5. Hence I1=I2=I3>I4, option C.
For a thin spherical shell rolling without slipping, I=2MR^2/3 and v=R*omega. Krot/Ktotal=(2/3)/(1+2/3)=2/5, so x=2.
S=n*(a+l)/2 gives 400=n*(5+45)/2=25n, hence n=16. A common difference of 8/3 is allowed.
